is acquiring privately held Calytrix Bio in a deal that could be worth up to $1.5B to the biotech focused on rare blood disorder treatments.
Calytrix will receive an unspecified upfront payment. The $1.5B value is based on that amount as well as achieving clinical and regulatory milestones.

The company's lead candidate is a biparatopic antibody for mutant calreticulin (mCALR)-driven essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis. "It is designed to deliver disease-modifying pan-mutant activity, with a safety and convenience profile that supports early intervention and long-term treatment," per a news release.
Calytrix was founded in 2025 by JP Morgan's
life sciences venture capital division, JP Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital.

title: Eli Lilly in up to $1.5B deal to acquire Calytrix Bio
